cases.text: Welcome everyone. Our appointment software is down, IT reported suspicious account activity, and the executive director is unavailable. We need to verify whether backups are restorable and check for data disclosure. Our choices are controlled continuity, technical checks first, or waiting for the director. Controlled continuity resumes appointments on paper right away. Technical checks first keeps appointments paused until systems are checked. Waiting delays any appointments and coordinator choice. How should we balance immediate service against technical verification?

cases.text: The recorded proposal for controlled continuity was approved. The board faced unavailable appointment software and an absent executive director. The decision appoints an interim incident coordinator, activates the approved paper appointment process, requires IT to verify backup usability before promising restoration, and mandates a factual public update. Possible tradeoffs exist across the options. Using paper appointments may sustain service delivery, but it could introduce administrative burdens. Keeping appointments paused for technical checks might protect data integrity, though it may delay community access. Waiting for the director could preserve original leadership, but it might stall coordinated action.

decision_prompt.text: Discussion is complete. Choose a response: A, controlled continuity with an interim coordinator and approved paper appointments; B, technical checks first while appointments remain paused; or C, wait for the director. Select your own vote. The CEO confirms the winning choice after everyone has voted.

transcript.name: Alex streaming CEO
transcript.text: The appointment system is unavailable and our director cannot coordinate this incident. The plan names no alternate. I propose that we appoint an interim coordinator now, so someone can organize the response. Who should take that role?

transcript.name: Morgan recorded participant
transcript.text: IT has reported suspicious account activity, but no disclosure is confirmed. Backup copies exist, yet restoration has not been checked. I want IT to verify backup usability, dependencies, and an estimate before we promise when appointments can resume.

transcript.name: Sam recorded participant
transcript.text: People still need appointments. I propose authorizing the service manager to use the approved paper process while technical checks continue. Our update should separate confirmed facts from unknowns and state when we will report again. Do you support that?

decisions.problem: How should the board respond to the service outage and unavailable director?

options.label: Controlled continuity
options.proposal: Appoint an interim incident coordinator, authorize the approved paper appointment process, ask IT to verify backup usability, recovery dependencies and a restoration estimate before any restoration promise, and issue a factual update that separates confirmed facts from unknowns and states the next update time.

options.label: Technical checks first
options.proposal: Appoint an interim incident coordinator, keep appointments paused until IT verifies recovery, and issue a factual update that separates confirmed facts from unknowns and states the next update time.

options.label: Wait for the director
options.proposal: Keep appointments paused and defer the interim coordinator appointment and paper appointment process while awaiting the director.

jobs.text:
The appointment system is unavailable and our director cannot coordinate this incident. The plan names no alternate. I propose that we appoint an interim coordinator now, so someone can organize the response. Who should take that role?

IT has reported suspicious account activity, but no disclosure is confirmed. Backup copies exist, yet restoration has not been checked. I want IT to verify backup usability, dependencies, and an estimate before we promise when appointments can resume.

People still need appointments. I propose authorizing the service manager to use the approved paper process while technical checks continue. Our update should separate confirmed facts from unknowns and state when we will report again. Do you support that?

jobs.question: Explain the recorded decision in the context of the problem. State whether the actual proposal was approved or rejected. Explain possible tradeoffs, explicitly as possibilities. Do not invent downstream outcomes or rewrite the committed decision.
jobs.text: The recorded proposal for controlled continuity was approved. The board faced unavailable appointment software and an absent executive director. The decision appoints an interim incident coordinator, activates the approved paper appointment process, requires IT to verify backup usability before promising restoration, and mandates a factual public update. Possible tradeoffs exist across the options. Using paper appointments may sustain service delivery, but it could introduce administrative burdens. Keeping appointments paused for technical checks might protect data integrity, though it may delay community access. Waiting for the director could preserve original leadership, but it might stall coordinated action.
